snippet.title: ‘Humiliated, scared, violated’ - family and friends of Brand accuser give evidence | Episode 8
snippet.description:

Sky News' Martin Brunt and Katie Spencer report more of the prosecution case against Russell Brand, as the family and friends of a woman who accuses him of rape in 2009 give evidence.

The woman claims she was anally raped by the comedian at his home. Her friends, family and colleagues have given their accounts of what she’d told them - including that she’d been "humiliated, scared, violated and in pain" after the alleged rape.

The defence cross-examined witnesses including the ex-boyfriend of the accuser, who they claimed had given conflicting statements to the police and the court.

Brand faces three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and one of indecent assault. He denies all the charges.

National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) experts are working with OpenAI, whose technology was used to discover the vulnerabilities, and partners around the globe to address potential problems, a No 10 spokeswoman said.

snippet.title: 🔴 VIVO | Los 7 políticos a los que Estados Unidos les quitó la VISA | Noticiero La FM 23-10-26
snippet.description:
🔴 EN VIVO | Noticias de Colombia y el mundo con Juan Lozano y la mesa de LA FM

La FM del 23 de octubre de 2026 abre con la noticia de que Estados Unidos revocó las visas de varios políticos colombianos, entre ellos Ricardo Roa, Yahir Acuña y Wadith Manzur, y con la reacción de congresistas que piden avanzar en los casos de corrupción. También recoge que el Gobierno expidió por decreto el Presupuesto General de la Nación 2027, por $634,9 billones, y que Alejandro Ordóñez llegó al Ministerio del Interior tras la renuncia de Rodrigo Lara. En orden público, informa del bombardeo en el Cauca donde murió alias Marcos Pacífico, de golpes contra el Clan del Golfo y de 142 extradiciones en 74 días de gobierno de Abelardo de la Espriella. En lo judicial, la Fiscalía incautó celulares en la investigación sobre la financiación de la consulta del Pacto Histórico. En salud, la ministra Ana María Vesga dice que liquidar las EPS intervenidas debe ser la última opción. Se suman la reconstrucción tras el terremoto en Pereira y Dosquebradas, las lluvias en el Meta, la reforma pensional, el alivio de intereses del Icetex y temas de Bogotá. La ronda internacional trata la detención de Luisa González en Ecuador, las deportaciones de Trump y las marchas en Venezuela. Las entrevistas incluyen el toque de queda en El Tarra (Catatumbo), los congresos de Asocajas y Camacol en Cartagena (este último con Leonardo Villar hablando de tasas de interés), las elecciones de medio término en EE. snippet.title: President Trump ordered to answer questions under oath in BBC lawsuit | BBC News
snippet.description:
A US judge has ordered President Donald Trump to answer questions under oath in his defamation lawsuit against the BBC by 11 December.
 
Trump is suing the BBC over an episode of Panorama that edited together two different sections of a speech he gave before the riot at the US Capitol in 2021.
 
Charles Tobin, a lawyer representing the BBC, said in court that "we still haven't been able to depose the plaintiff" with two months left in the discovery period, during which both sides are legally required to exchange information with each other on their case.
 
Trump cancelled a previous deposition on 16 October, citing "matters of national importance" while he was campaigning in Georgia.
 
The judge in the case, US Magistrate Judge Enjoliqué Lett, said that Trump must sit for the deposition by 11 December, unless the discovery period is extended.

 The costume drama series, Downton Abbey, written and created by Oscar-winning writer Julian Fellowes, stars Academy Award-winner Maggie Smith as a Dowager Countess of an Edwardian English country house in 1912. The all-star cast also includes Hugh Bonneville and Elizabeth McGovern.
